 Why in news? 
 Children's Day 2026 will be celebrated across India on 14 November 2026 (Saturday) . The day is popularly known as Bal Diwas . 
 History of Children's Day in India 
 14 November 1889: Jawaharlal Nehru was born in Allahabad (present-day Prayagraj), Uttar Pradesh. 
 He became independent India's first Prime Minister in 1947. 
 Nehru was popularly known as Chacha Nehru because of his affection for children. 
 Children's Day was associated with 14 November during Nehru's lifetime. His 1957 speech explicitly referred to the occasion as Children's Day. 
 After his death on 27 May 1964 , 14 November continued to be commemorated as Children's Day in his memory. 
 Why is Children's Day Celebrated? 
 Promoting Education: Ensuring access to quality education for every child. 
 Child Protection: Preventing child labour, child trafficking, abuse and exploitation. 
 Health and Nutrition: Improving children's healthcare, nutrition and overall well-being. 
 Equal Opportunities: Ensuring that every child gets equal opportunities irrespective of gender, caste, economic background or disability. 
 Awareness of Child Rights : Educating society about the rights and dignity of children.

 National Policy for Children, 2013 
 The Government of India adopted the National Policy for Children on 26 April 2013 . 
 It recognises every person below 18 years of age as a child. 
 The policy identifies four major priority areas: 
 Survival : Right to life and survival. 
 Health and Nutrition : Access to healthcare and adequate nutrition. 
 Education and Development: Opportunities for education and overall development. 
 Protection and Participation: Protection against exploitation and the right to participate in decisions affecting children.

 Major Challenges Related to Child Welfare in India 
 Child Labour: Children continue to face economic exploitation and loss of educational opportunities. 
 Child Marriage: Early marriage affects education, health and personal development, particularly among girls. 
 Child Abus e: Physical, emotional and sexual abuse threaten children's safety. 
 Gender Discrimination: Unequal opportunities affect girls' education, nutrition and development. 
 School Dropouts : Poverty, lack of infrastructure and social barriers affect educational continuity.

 FAQs 
 When is Children's Day celebrated in India? 
 14 November 
 Who adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child? 
 The United Nations General Assembly in 1989. 
 What is the legal definition of a child under the National Policy for Children, 2013? 
 Every person below 18 years of age. 
 Which constitutional amendment introduced Article 21A? 
 The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. 
 Which organisation is responsible for monitoring child rights protection laws in India? 
 The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR).
